hints.title: Multi-Stream Candidate Merging Obstacle
hints.text: Every ugly number after 1 is generated by multiplying an earlier ugly number by 2, 3, or 5. How can multiple tracking indices generate them in ascending order?

hints.title: Independent Factor Pointer Invariant
hints.text: Advance indices corresponding to each prime factor independently whenever their product matches the minimum next candidate to avoid duplicates.

hints.title: Three Pointer Value Progression Procedure
hints.text: Initialize an array of size n with first value 1 and three pointer indices set to 0. At each step from 1 to n - 1, compute candidates by multiplying pointers by 2, 3, and 5. Set the next element to the minimum candidate, and advance all pointer indices that produced that value. Return the n-th element.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: input element count or target integer bound
complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N) time and O(N) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Checking every consecutive integer for the ugly property tests many non-ugly numbers, taking exponential time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Three-pointer generation computes ugly numbers directly in O(N) time using O(N) array storage.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should advance all pointers matching the chosen minimum to avoid duplicating values (e.g. 2 * 3 == 3 * 2).
